conclusion: CC is the common genotype at SIRT6 rs117385980 and carries no T allele. Neither study that examined this variant reports an effect for CC beyond the absence of T: Hirvonen et al. describe a trend consistent with CC being the ordinary genotype rather than an advantageous one. No positive longevity claim is made for this genotype.

CT carriers of SIRT6 rs117385980 were under-represented among the longest-lived in both cohorts that have examined this variant, but NEITHER RESULT IS STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT. Hirvonen et al. 2017 (Finnish men, n=198 combined) report OR 3.58 (95% CI 0.96-13.4, p=0.074) for the T allele in men who died younger versus long-lived men; Sheikholmolouki et al. 2025 (Iranian adults 60-90, n=227) found no T allele at all in the 80-90 age group versus 1.39% at 60-69 and 4.65% at 70-79 (p=0.073), and found NO association with frailty (adjusted OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.10-9.66, p=0.98). Both are small, both are under-powered (Hirvonen report 28.4% power), and both are ancestry-specific. Treat this as a suggestive trend from two cohorts, not an established effect.
negatives: The same T allele was ABSENT from the frail group in Sheikholmolouki et al. 2025 and its carrier frequency was highest in the robust group, so any adverse reading for longevity is not mirrored in that study's frailty analysis.
